channel.title: Making of Iltonggi
channel.description: How Iltonggi is being made — one short note a day.

item.title: A Name and a Record, Nicknames and the Scoreboard
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: How the nickname and the records screen in Iltonggi work, what the four scoreboards count, and what is still being prepared.

item.title: Ask Before You Pass, the Landowners of Act 10
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: Act 10 of Iltonggi has regions you cannot attack, and the reasons we turned a conquest game into a game of asking first.

item.title: Two Brothers and One Table, Choosing a Side in Act 9
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: How Act 9 of Iltonggi turns a family quarrel in the Andes into a choice about which brother you stand beside.

item.title: City on the Lake, What We Chose Not to Draw
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: Act 8 of Iltonggi, a map set on a lake in the highlands, and the lines we drew around what we would leave out of the picture.

item.title: Three Seas, and the Cliff We Found by Simulation
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: Acts 4 to 6 in Iltonggi, and what two hundred simulated games per difficulty taught us about balance.

item.title: From Three Kingdoms to a Wider Map, Where Iltonggi Stands Now
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: A plain look at how the acts of Iltonggi have grown beyond the Korean peninsula, what the world map does, and what is still being worked on.

item.title: Your First 20 Turns, Five Things to Watch Early in a Land Grab
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: How to use troops, actions, scouting and diplomacy in your first Iltonggi game, with a focus on the early flow.

item.title: From War Drums to Gayageum, We Made the Sounds Ourselves
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: How Iltonggi's 15 effects and 4 music tracks were synthesized by script with no outside audio, and why we remade some of them.

item.title: Daegaya, 562: The Year the Last Gaya Closed
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: Eight years after Daegaya stood with Baekje at Gwansanseong, this is how the records say it fell to Silla in 562, and what kind of kingdom Gaya is in Iltonggi.

item.title: The Day After You Take a Town: Designing the Aftermath of Conquest
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: What happens to population and mood right after you take a town in Iltonggi, and why we made sure that winning the battle is not the end of it.

item.title: Hanji, Ink and the Seal: Choosing a Face for the Map
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: The materials and rules behind three look drafts for Iltonggi's map, redrawing the same land as clay wall, hanji paper and an old surveyor's sheet.

item.title: Gwansanseong, 554: Where an Alliance Ended
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: Three years after the 551 Han River scenario, the Baekje-Silla alliance broke at Gwansanseong. Here is that scene, and where Iltonggi's diplomacy rules touch it.

item.title: Keeping Direct Command From Becoming a Cheat: Balancing It by Computer
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: How we keep Direct Command in Iltonggi from becoming a cheat by balancing it with simulated battles, why its rules stay simple, and what is still left to do.

item.title: The 551 Han River Contest: Unnamed Generals Become "General ○○"
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: Building Iltonggi's 551 Han River scenario: dropping out-of-era generals, placing Kim Mu-ryeok and the Daegaya king, and why unknown names stay "General ○○."

item.title: Four Kingdoms, Four Colors, Still Distinct at Night
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: How we picked colors for Goguryeo, Baekje, Silla and Gaya in Iltonggi, measured whether they stay distinct day and night, and added hanja chips and shapes too.

item.title: A Three Kingdoms Land Grab for Your Phone
item.dc:creator: ipe Studio
item.description: Why we're building Iltonggi, a Three Kingdoms land-grab game for your phone: 5-10 minute rounds, autosave, a short first game, and no daily log-in pressure.
